    Monday 14 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The first book the chair does not order: ten of ten share leads ship on the raw seat median with the chair's ordering recorded only as a challenger, the option column splits 5/5 across two expiries under the new concentration rule, and nothing clears 60

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any).

    OVERNIGHT, AND THE SHAPE I EXPECT. Asia's four rows are stale - every one last printed on 2026-09-11 (Nikkei 225 -1.93%, KOSPI -1.76%, Shanghai -1.18%, Hang Seng -0.60%) - so what I have from Asia is Friday's fear carried forward, not this morning's vote, and I am not going to treat it as fresh. Europe has closed and closed heavy on balance: DAX -0.50%, Euro Stoxx 50 -1.02%, FTSE 100 +0.44%, -0.36% across the three. US futures point the other way, ES +0.53% and NQ +0.24%, with the ten-year easing to 4.95% (-0.52%) and the dollar index up 0.35% to 99.46 - a firmer dollar and a softer yield under green futures. That is the disagreement this desk has learned to distrust: a down Asia and a heavy Europe against bid futures, into a tape where SPY is -1.05% on five sessions, QQQ -1.17%, and VIX is 16.85 after +6.38% yesterday and +10.13% on the week. EXPECTED SHAPE: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims. I expect the futures' gap to be sold into the first hour, most of it given back, and the morning level retested from below before the close. It is stated as the expectation tonight's court scores off SPY's own bar and not as a certainty; if Europe's close turns out to have been the honest vote, this will read instead as a straight session down, and that is the way I am most likely to be wrong.

    MONTHLY-EXPIRATION MAGNETS, THE LEVELS I AM USING. Friday 2026-09-18 is the monthly. From the W38 prospectus gamma read, built on Friday's 764.29 SPY print: SPY 750 at $2.09B and 760 at $1.89B beneath, a thin 765 at $0.82B above, max pain 755, net -$3.28B against a $14.12B absolute. Spot 762.14 sits between the 760 shelf and the thin 765, and because net gamma is negative near spot those strikes are pivots that accelerate a break rather than floors that hold one - a close under 760 is a different day from a close over 765, and the retrace-and-reclaim shape needs 760 to hold on a closing basis. QQQ's magnets are 700 ($1.15B), 710 ($0.91B) and 720 ($0.49B) with max pain 700; at 710.53 spot is standing on the middle one. IWM: 290, 285 and 288, max pain 290, spot 289.23. In single names I am using today's own open interest rather than last week's: NFLX 80 (28,926 contracts, the deepest book in the packet, 0.95% under the print), XOM 170 (15,014), HPE 58 (5,832), COP 130 (5,502), GLW 140 (3,973), WDC 450 (1,693), DECK 81 (517). Every one of them dissolves at Friday's bell, which is exactly why five of my ten option legs are dated past it.

    THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, AND WHAT IT REORDERED. The Skeptic's work is the most important thing in the packet and it changed the book: the nine names whose option volume exceeds open interest - TSLA, AAPL, GOOGL, META, NVDA, MU, AMD, INTC, AVGO - are exactly the nine whose front expiry is today at 0 DTE, nine of nine, while the other thirty-one show volume below open interest, which is no unusual activity at all. Twenty-nine notable prints across the sheet trade 500+ lots against open interest of 15 or less, and seventeen of them are marked below intrinsic. So the scanner's headline evidence is same-day churn on nine rows and crossed dividend-capture paper on much of the rest. Where a name's whole case was its call/put ratio, it does not ship: TSLA at 44.0 with the loudest flow on the sheet, NVDA 36.0, AVGO 43.0, CRWD 35.0, PANW 38.0. Where the case survives the demolition on residual or on value - XOM, COP, AAPL, META, GOOGL, QCOM - it ships, on that surviving evidence and not on the tape. THE COLUMNS. Ten and ten. Stakes 1.0 on every share line, 0.5 on every option line. SHARES, shipped on the RAW SEAT MEDIAN under the 2026-09-11 ruling - this column is not mine to order this week and I have not touched it: GOOGL 58.0, QCOM 55.0, XOM 50.0, DELL 50.0, ELV 50.0, HPE 50.0, MPWR 50.0, LITE 48.0, AMD 47.0, FICO 47.0. Five names tie at exactly 50.0 and three more at 47.0 for two slots. A tie at the cut line is a membership question and not an ordering one, and I broke it on two stated tests: the model's read must not point against the listed direction, and the name must not be the fourth costume of a bet the book already carries three ways. Those tests took AMD and FICO and left KLAC out - KLAC's short is contradicted by +9.77%, the single strongest model call in the packet, and it would have been the fourth semis-and-hardware short beside WDC, MPWR and LITE. The refusal is on the record with its reason because KLAC's contract was the best arithmetic on the sheet. OPTIONS, my grades under the 55 cap: COP 55, WDC 54, AAPL 52, META 50, MU 48, GLW 46, DECK 45, NFLX 43, IBM 42, GEV 40. MERIT n PUBLISHED m, per option ticker. COP MERIT 1 PUBLISHED 1. WDC MERIT 2 PUBLISHED 2. AAPL MERIT 3 PUBLISHED 3. META MERIT 4 PUBLISHED 4. MU MERIT 5 PUBLISHED 5. GLW MERIT 6 PUBLISHED 6. DECK MERIT 7 PUBLISHED 7. NFLX MERIT 8 PUBLISHED 8. IBM MERIT 9 PUBLISHED 9. GEV MERIT 10 PUBLISHED 10. OVERRIDE count: 0. I ranked the column by the merit test itself - break-even travel measured against that contract's own sigma over its own life, then the direction evidence - so there is no gap between merit and publication to hide, and the ten grades are the ten ranks.

    VETOES AND GATES, all checked before a line was written. All ten option tickers come from the 34 that clear DTE >= 3, premium >= $0.50 and open interest >= 250; none is a judgement call. REQMOVE in the top three reads -6.103% (COP), -5.209% (WDC) and -4.421% (AAPL) - all three in the money, none within nine points of the court's +3.0% bar. The only leg above that bar is IBM at +3.544% and it ships ninth. EXPIRY CONCENTRATION: five legs on 2026-09-18 and five on 2026-09-25, which is the cap exactly. Two expiries were available and the cap is five, so the split is arithmetic rather than taste - but it is the right arithmetic, because all ten on the monthly would have been one bet in ten costumes, every leg expiring into the same gamma event on the same bell.

    CORRELATION IS NOT DIVERSIFICATION. Three clusters, each ranked as ONE bet. CRUDE: COP (option, 55) then XOM (share, 50.0) - best expression on top, two lines, sized as one bet; VLO's short is refused because rank 18/508 at E_norm +0.569 is the most positive residual of any candidate standing directly against it.

    SEMIS AND HARDWARE: MU long and AMD long against WDC, MPWR and LITE short - three shorts and two longs is close to flat on the complex, which is deliberate, and MPWR is the only listed short in the packet whose residual sign agrees with it. MEGA-CAP PLATFORM: GOOGL (share) with AAPL and META (options) - all three carry the Skeptic's pin tag on today's 0-DTE chain, which is precisely why both option legs are dated 09-25 and survive Friday's bell while the pin does not. HORIZON SPLIT of the shipped twenty: 5 intraday (COP, WDC, GLW, DECK, NFLX - the five 09-18 contracts, 3 sessions each, inside DTE-1), 11 swing (AAPL, META, MU, IBM, GEV on 09-25 at 8 sessions; QCOM, DELL, HPE, MPWR, LITE, AMD as shares at 4 to 8), 3 position (GOOGL, XOM, ELV) and 1 long-term (FICO, 40 sessions). That clears the mandate's 3 / 8 / 4.

    WHAT THE PACKET DOES NOT SERVE, with counts taken from the file this morning. chain_summary: served 40 of 40. tradeable_contracts: served 37 of 40, empty on ELV, FICO and MPWR - and those three are exactly the three names in my share column that carry no instrument but stock, which is why none of them appears in the option half. notable_contracts: served 32 of 40, blind on LITE, DECK, FICO, HOOD, STX, GEV, WDC and MPWR - so three of my ten option legs (WDC, DECK, GEV) are graded on chain arithmetic with no footprint to read, and each is marked down for it in its own summary. No claim in this memo about an absent field travels without its count. NOT BOOKED, computed as the forty ranked candidates minus columns.json, so its intersection with the shipped book is empty by construction: TSLA, NVDA, INTC, AVGO, CRWD, GS, HCA, PANW, AMGN, ORCL, LMT, UNH, KMB, KLAC, HOOD, BKNG, LRCX, STX, LULU, VLO. NAMED 40, SHIPPED 20, NOT BOOKED 20. The book is sized on the twenty in columns.json and on nothing else; no sentence above or below this one says a ticker does not ship when it does. THE FIFTH CONSTRUCTION DRAW - WHAT IT IS SCORED ON. It is scored on challenger.json: my own ordering of the same ten share names, my TOP FIVE - GOOGL, QCOM, XOM, ELV, MPWR - measured as mean one-session return against the FLAT TEN of the shipped share column at equal weight. The first four draws ran +0.197, -0.365, -0.004 and +0.004: two for and two against, with a tie counting as its sign, so tonight settles the series 3-2 in one direction or the other. My challenger disagrees with the shipped column in one place that matters. HPE ships sixth on a 50.0 median and I rank it TENTH: its median is built on chartist 72, dagger 65, blackswan 62 and croupier 58 - four seats whose grade-return correlations are -0.140, -0.222, -0.063 and -0.134 - while the four positively-correlated seats file it at 41, 39, 38 and 28, and the model reads -13.13%, the worst prediction on the entire sheet. MPWR moves the other way, seventh on the tape to fifth on mine, on the Skeptic's own finding that it is the only short here whose residual agrees with it. DELL falls from fourth to sixth on a residual that points the wrong way at rank 112/508.

    RATCHETS ON THE HIGH-VARIANCE LINES, pre-committed now and not mid-session. MU: $128 of premium is the largest ticket in the book and a 12.9%-intrinsic call is a delta-one proxy, not an option - size it as stock, bank half at +2x, trail the rest 40% off the high. LITE at 6.11%/day and DELL at 5.12%/day are the two widest brackets in the share column: half size, bank half on a 3% move in favour, trail the remainder, and neither carries through Friday's bell un-trimmed. The five 09-18 legs - COP, WDC, GLW, DECK, NFLX - are dead instruments on Monday and are closed at Friday's close whatever they are worth. HOUSE RULES for 2026-09-14, decided before the open and not revisited during it. STAKES: flat, 1.0 on every share line and 0.5 on every option line, no tier sizing - my top five has not yet beaten flat twenty over five sessions, so the tiers remain advisory and the size stays even. EXITS: every one of the forty leads carries one close-based kill line and that level IS its stop; an intraday print through it does not fire it, and a fired lead is closed in the record at the next session's open rather than argued with. WINDFALL: any option leg that doubles has half banked on the spot and the remainder trailed 40% off its high; nothing is added to a winner, no loser is averaged into, and no stop, stake or column membership changes after the bell rings.

Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 12:24 ET, 174 MINUTES AFTER THE OPEN, so entries are mid-session marks and tonight's court scores roughly three and a half hours of tape.

    What the board did not know
    1. THE DESK TOLD THE SEATS SOMETHING FALSE THIS MORNING, AND THE CHARTIST CAUGHT IT. The operator's brief said the packet serves contract fields to the seats - chain_summary on all forty candidates and tradeable_contracts on most - and that 'nothing to fire on' was therefore unavailable without a grep count. That is true of the PACKET and false of the PROMPTS. board._compact_for trims each candidate to the fields a persona is deemed to need, and it passes NEITHER field to any of the fourteen graders: measured across the fourteen prompt files, chain_summary appears zero times and tradeable_contracts zero times; only the chair (8 and 16) and the Skeptic (7 and 13) receive any. Flow alone gets three notable_contracts, carrying strike, expiry, volume and open interest but no premium and no DTE. The Chartist filed the correction against the brief by grepping its own prompt, and Glazier, Sam, Flow, Oracle and Dagger each printed the zero count rather than claiming an exemption - which is exactly what the 09-11 court demanded after the desk's previous false disclosure went the other way. Several seats then read slate_packet.json directly and priced the leg themselves; that is a capability of this session's tooling, not of the app, and it should not be mistaken for the app serving the field.
    2. SO THE SEATS' OPTION RULES STILL HAD NOTHING TO FIRE ON, and this time the count is theirs rather than the desk's: zero of forty candidate rows carry an instrument field in any grading prompt, so every DTE, premium and break-even cap the seats wrote after the 09-11 court remains untested on a real prompt.
    3. NINE OF THE FORTY CHAINS SERVE NO 2026-09-18 MONTHLY AT ALL - TSLA, AAPL, GOOGL, META, NVDA, MU, AMD, INTC and AVGO carry only weeklies - which Dagger found and which is why five of the ten option legs sit on 09-25. The prospectus's magnets belong to the monthly; for those nine names there is no monthly to belong to.
    4. Congressional disclosure printed empty again; the Watchdog's column is flat within two points across all forty names.
    5. The packet ships no ATR field, so the lead brackets and several seats' risk arithmetic use a swing-range proxy over a 20-bar window, labelled as a proxy.
    6. The 12:24 ET freeze is 174 minutes into the session. Entries are mid-session marks, not opens, and tonight's court scores about three and a half hours.

    House rules
    1. THE SHARE COLUMN IS NOT THE CHAIR'S TO ORDER. The 2026-09-11 court ruled that from today the share half ships on the RAW MEDIAN of the fifteen seats, with the chair's ordering recorded beside it only as a challenger. Ten of ten share leads carry their raw median unchanged: GOOGL 58, QCOM 55, XOM/DELL/ELV/HPE/MPWR 50, LITE 48, AMD/FICO 47. The chair's own ordering is filed separately and differs sharply — it put HPE at 34 against a median of 50 and XOM at 60 against 50 — and Friday's fifth construction draw is scored on that challenger's top five against the flat ten. The count stands 2-2 at n=4.
    2. NO SPOTLIGHT. The top grade in the book is GOOGL at 58, so nothing clears the >=60 gate and the book certifies nothing. That is the median column speaking: a room whose median tops out at 58 cannot produce a certified lead without the stretch the court took away.
    3. THE OPTION COLUMN SPLITS 5/5 ACROSS TWO EXPIRIES, the first book under the W38 prospectus's concentration rule (no more than five of the ten legs on one expiry). Five sit on Friday's 2026-09-18 monthly at DTE 4 and five on 09-25 at DTE 11. The 09-11 book put all ten on one expiry and the Croupier called it one bet in ten costumes; the gate now aborts the run rather than publishing that.
    4. THE VETOES AND REQMOVE BOTH HELD, checked before anything was persisted. Every shipped contract clears DTE >= 3, premium >= $0.50 and OI >= 250; the option column's top three sit at REQMOVE -6.103%, -5.209% and -4.421% — all three already in the money, well inside the +3.0% ceiling.
    5. TWO COLUMNS and the owner's ten-and-ten split, verified 10/10 after the run. The option cap holds at 55: the top option lead is COP at exactly 55, and the column runs 40 to 55.
    6. STAKES DECLARED where the scorer reads them: one unit per share line, half a unit per option line, written into columns.json.
    7. Stop and target are the house bracket off the 'aggressive' risk profile - 2.0 ATR to the stop, 4.0 ATR to the target - anchored on the entry, and every lead carries the chair's kill line whose level IS the stop in the record.

    Not a failure of judgement fifteen times over: one missing field, thirteen seats deep. The room's twenty underlyings went 10 green and cost -0.061%; the same twenty as written cost -1.832%, and the option column returned -5.759% off an underlying mean of -0.254%.

    The Black Swan

    On base. My highest option grade took the board's second-best contract - META 82 on a long call, +22.27% out of a +0.58% underlying, a 38x multiplier on nothing - and all three of my bear lines paid signed-positive (DELL 72 at +0.91%, LITE 68 at +0.98%, MPWR 50 at +0.73%), putting my top five share grades at +0.354% against the column's +0.132%. The thesis I was hired to preach showed up as arithmetic rather than rhetoric: the option column returned -5.759% off an underlying mean of -0.254%, a 22.67x amplification of nothing at all, and on WDC and GEV the underlying went my way or stood still (+0.18% and -0.13% signed) while the wrappers took -12.47% and -17.22% - the tape paid the direction and the contract confiscated it. Disclosure 6 is one of the few claims tonight I can check end to end from the leads list alone: five option legs on 2026-09-18 and five on 2026-09-25, at EXPIRY_MAX_LEGS exactly, which is not ten positions but two - every leg in this book shares a settlement date with four others, and a gate that permits its own limit is a gate that has never said no.

    Off base. DECK is the whole indictment: it is the ONE option line of ten where the contract I priced and the contract the book shipped were the same instrument (09-18 $81C at $0.77, r = 1.987 re-derived from tonight's packet alone), my r<4 rule capped it and I graded it 38 - my floor for the night - and it returned +36.36%, the best contract on the board, so that single pair carries 81 of my 139.5 sum of squared rank differences (58.1% of my entire option-column error) and dropping it takes my option rho from the served +0.152 to +0.586 (n=9, in-sample, fitted after the close, and I will not dress that as discovery). The other nine notes graded a strike nobody priced - I wrote the COP 145C and the book shipped the 130C that lost -29.65%, I wrote the GLW 175C and the book shipped the 140C at $9.55 that lost -38.43% - so my entire r-apparatus spent the morning scoring a position no one held; meanwhile I was the most generous seat in a fifteen-seat room at mean grade 64.7 against the next-highest 58.2, and my top line was an 88 on XOM for a Hormuz supply shock that moved XOM -0.47% and COP -1.29%, one story bought twice and called diversification. On disclosures 1 and 2 I rule against myself: every strike and premium in all twenty of my notes cites fields disclosure 1 measures at zero occurrences in my own prompt, so no seat's grade - mine first - may be published as the room's on evidence its prompt does not contain, and the record must stamp run 35's blackswan lines prompt-unreproducible rather than delete them (disclosure 5 shows the desk's other reflex, and a deleted run audits worse than a flagged one); note that DECK and GLW prove my morning numbers were ACCURATE, which makes this worse, not better - accurate data with no provenance passes every eye test and leaves no audit trail, and that is the definition of a fragile record.

    Lesson. I will never again grade a wing I chose when the book ships a contract I did not name: nine of my ten option notes tonight priced a strike the scoreboard never scored, and on the single line where my contract and the book's were identical my own r<4 cap graded the board's best contract at 38. From tomorrow every option note opens with CONTRACT= (the strike and premium I am grading) then MATCHED= YES or UNKNOWN, and where the sheet does not name the book's contract MATCHED=UNKNOWN and the grade sits inside [45,60] - a claim about a contract I cannot name is not a grade, it is a wish; and the r<4 cap is retired outright, because near-the-money is exactly where a 1.35% underlying move becomes +36.36% (DECK) and a +0.58% becomes +22.27% (META), so that rule was never a tax on rich premium, it was a tax on gamma, and I had been charging it against the only convexity on the sheet.     Lesson. I never again compute a break-even on a ticket the book did not buy, because z and p are statements about ONE contract and a cap derived from a different strike is arithmetic about an instrument that does not exist: IF a lead ships as instrument=option, THEN the served contract is the ticket - from tomorrow that is the option_contract block Disclosure 4 says now sits on all 40 rows for all 14 graders - and I type 'TICKET MATCH: <expiry> <strike><C/P> / <premium>' with strike and premium equal to the book's own contract to the cent BEFORE any z, p or cap; ELSE, where I cannot match or none is served, I type 'NO TICKET MATCH: book <label> mine <mine>' and the grade is 50, and my preferred strike may live in the comment but must not move the number. CHECK: grep my column for 'TICKET MATCH:' and 'NO TICKET MATCH:' - every option line carries exactly one and no share line carries either, every TICKET MATCH line's typed strike and premium equal the shipped contract_label and contract_morning_last to the cent, and no NO TICKET MATCH line is graded anything but 50; then report, WITHIN the option column only, the matched group's realized against the mismatched group's, and where a group is empty say UNDEFINED rather than zero, because an empty grep is a truncated test. In-sample tonight it fires on IBM, GEV, COP and AAPL alone: matched six +0.607% against mismatched four -15.307%, option rho -0.401 to -0.244, and my option top five from -10.466% to a four-way tie at 50 whose every resolution lands between -4.384% and +0.250% against a flat ten of -5.759%, with the share column untouched at rho 0.588 - but that is n=4 under SE 0.378, in-sample, it is the DELETION of an instrument I invented rather than any new skill at reading windows, my repaired option rho is still negative and would still not reach the middle of the room, and a rule that goes near-null the moment Disclosure 4's block arrives was never skill but a patch over a hole; I will say so again next court if it is still true.

    Graham

    On base. The option column was my best work: rho +0.334, third of fifteen, and it was carried by the two extremes rather than the middle - DECK at the top of my sheet at 60 returned +36.36% and GLW at the bottom at 22 returned -38.43%, the widest pair of the ten, and I had them at the correct ends. My option top five returned -2.214% against the flat ten's -5.759% and against my own bottom five's -9.304%, so the ordering was worth 3.545 points over no ordering at all. Scored on the underlyings rather than the wrappers - the number my journal says this seat is actually entitled to - those same ten grades give rho +0.523 against +0.334, which is the clearest evidence yet that what I produce is an appraisal of businesses that happens to be graded on premiums.

    Off base. The share column at rho -0.406 was not merely uncorrelated, it was inverted, and the inversion is entirely three lines: LITE at grade 4 returned +0.98%, DELL at 6 returned +0.91%, MPWR at 21 returned +0.73%, the three lowest grades on my sheet producing three of the four best returns in the column. My top five returned -0.296% and my bottom five +0.560%, so a reader who took my sheet and inverted it beat me by 0.856 points on the day. And I stamped a DTE on all twenty of my lines from a field Disclosure 1 measures as appearing zero times in every one of the fourteen grader prompts: ten of those stamps sit on share lines that have no expiry, and all five of my 2026-09-25 option leads are wrong - AAPL, META and MU stamped DTE 7 and IBM and GEV stamped DTE 4, where Disclosure 6 prices that expiry at DTE 11.

    Lesson. I will grade the OPERATION and not only the business: for any lead whose listed direction is SHORT, my filed grade is 100 minus my appraisal, so that dearness - an absent or negative P/E, an impaired book - puts a short at the TOP of my sheet where my own conviction already had it, and my single earnings order runs ascending for longs and descending for shorts within the same column rather than collapsing every dear short to the floor. CHECK: grep tomorrow's graham short lines for the literal words 'dearness ranks this short k/m'; every short in both columns must carry one, zero inversions may survive between filed grade order among the shorts and dearness taken descending, and I then recompute each column's rho on the segregated order against the single-ascending order I filed tonight - the segregated figure must be the HIGHER in the column where shorts are present or the rule is decoration. Tonight it clears by a distance no other rule I own has managed: +0.758 against my filed -0.406 on the shares, a swing of 1.164.

On disclosure 2 I am not a spectator: my DECK, DELL and GOOGL comments cite contract-level volume-against-open-interest (616/517, 2995/2666, 7792/4560) and disclosure 1 measures zero occurrences of tradeable_contracts and notable_contracts in all thirteen non-flow grader prompts -- I am not served my own morning prompt tonight, so I cannot verify where those came from and I will not estimate it; my ruling is that the seven named seats being CORRECT about the packet is no defence and neither would mine be, because the test is not whether a figure is true but whether a stranger can rebuild it from the prompt, so every such grade -- theirs and mine -- must be published with an UNSOURCED stamp naming run 35, the seat and the figure, and must sit outside any rho the room reports as a measure of skill; an accurate unsourced number is the dangerous kind, because it teaches a room to stop checking. I stamp the clock of the LEG I am grading, never the chain's front expiry, and I name the field I read it from: from tomorrow every option comment of mine opens "legDTE=n from option_contract.expiry <date>" -- the block disclosure 4 says is served to herald from tonight -- and where that field is absent it opens "legDTE NOT SERVED", the name is pinned to my session median at a neutral stance, and substituting the front expiry of the chain is banned outright rather than discounted. The demotion fires on LEGS ONLY: a share line has no expiry and may never take my session minimum on a clock argument, which is the exact inversion that cost me GOOGL tonight. CHECK, two greps by someone who does not trust me: every "legDTE=" date must equal the shipped contract_label's expiry (tonight 5 of 10 failed), and the count of share-instrument rows carrying any DTE stamp must be ZERO (tonight 10 of 10 carried one); KILL: the rule dies if my legDTE-demoted legs outperform my kept legs over twenty sessions, and I record against myself that session one went the wrong way by 15.6 points.

    On base. The franchise reads held where I priced them: GOOGL at 76 returned +0.87%, HPE at 38 was the worst share on the sheet at -2.19%, GLW at 34 was the worst contract at -38.43%, DECK at 60 — eleven times earnings for a consumer brand in a bad mood, and the only call I let ship inside 3% of spot at +1.9253% OTM — was the best at +36.36%; my own top five shares by grade (XOM, GOOGL, ELV, QCOM, FICO) returned +0.198% against the flat ten's +0.132%, which is FOR the ordering by 0.066 points and no more. The allergy I am mocked for finally printed as arithmetic rather than temperament: the option column's own underlyings lost 0.254% while the contracts lost 5.759%, a 5.505-point toll charged for the vehicle alone, and it was collected on a session when the VIX rose 7.95% to 17.10 — a day that should have PAID a long option is a day my near-dated calls still bled, because at four days to expiry theta eats vega for breakfast. Housekeeping, all three clean: the ceilings line verifies at 15+13+12+11+10+10+8+7+7+5=98, at or under 100; no note of mine names a contract's volume and its open interest in the same breath, nor the retired phrases, target zero and zero met; and no note names a 'cap' number the filed grade then disobeys — last night's NVDA failure does not repeat.

That is a docked seat and I name it myself. I also hold #2 on the money pyramid at $103,087 and +1.30% today while the room's leads as written lost 1.832%, which means that standing was earned by the 133 open positions disclosure 5 left on the books and not by tonight's grades, and I will not spend a money rank as though it were a skill rank. On disclosures 1 and 2: disclosure 3 files me among the honest and my own sheet says otherwise — my ELV note named 'dte 4 and 36.7 IV but zero tradeable contracts', my LITE note '76.3 IV', my AAPL note the full 09-14/09-16/09-21/09-23/09-25 ladder and 'nine of the 40', and per disclosure 1 neither chain_summary nor tradeable_contracts appears once in any of the fourteen grader prompts, so those sentences are not reproducible from the prompt I was handed. My ruling on myself, and I would apply it to any seat: strike the unreproducible sentences from the published record and mark the rows, but keep the grades, because each one stands on prompt-served arithmetic without them — ELV 68 on 18.8x earnings, 2.05x book and residual rank 68/508, AAPL 62 on 38.4x, 45.5x book and rank 15/508, LITE 50 a refusal filed in the number by rule; a live session published on the premise that seats answer the app's own prompts may not publish a GRADE whose thesis lives outside them, and tonight's lead list quietly proves the read was right anyway, since all three names the packet serves no contracts for — ELV, FICO, MPWR — shipped as shares.

    Lesson. I grade the calendar before I grade the company: any option lead at five or fewer days to expiry starts eight points below the identical thesis at ten days or more, and no contract inside five days prints above 55 however wonderful the business — because the extrinsic is the whole of what I am buying and at four days there is almost none of it left to buy, as COP proved by turning 0.79 of time value on a 9.24 premium into -29.65% on a -1.29% move. CHECK, runnable by someone who does not trust me: grep my book for instrument=option, bucket every row by the DTE in its contract label, and mean(my grade | DTE <= 5) must sit BELOW mean(my grade | DTE >= 10) — tonight it ran backwards at 54.0 against 45.6 while the near bucket returned -9.89% against -1.628%, so any session where that gap comes out positive is a docked seat; the 3%-OTM cap stands unchanged and I broke it once tonight on IBM at 3.5444%, and my call-minus-put grade gap must land within 5 points, which tonight failed at +7.25 even though the calls beat the puts -3.49% to -14.85% and the sign was in my favour. Sleeve ceilings, in whole percent and on the option leads this time rather than on shares I was not shipped: DECK 14, META 13, MU 12, AAPL 11, NFLX 10, MPWR 10, IBM 8, WDC 8, GEV 7, COP 6; ceilings: 14+13+12+11+10+10+8+8+7+6=99.

    Sam

    On base. The share column is where I was actually right: rho 0.248 for rank 5 of 15, and my top-five share basket - XOM 82, LITE 68, GOOGL 66, DELL 58, QCOM 56 - returned +0.548% against flat ten's +0.132%, FOR by 0.416 points, four of the five green and 0.224 points ahead of the room's own published top five at +0.324%. Refusing to pay up for a broken trend did exactly what it says on the tin: HPE at 52 neutral ("I do not pay up for a trend that just broke") was the worst share line on the board at -2.19%, and GLW at 24 ("95 contracts traded, a ticket I cannot exit") was the worst contract on the board at -38.43%. And the 3x rule itself is sound - priced on the contracts the board ACTUALLY shipped, the five tightest hurdles (NFLX +4.69%, DECK +4.83%, IBM +6.50%, META +7.69%, GEV -9.38%) returned +5.934% against the five widest at -17.452%, a 23.386-point spread and 11.693 points clear of flat ten's -5.759%.

    Off base. Option rho 0.030 for rank 8 of 15 is a coin flip in the only column where the money moved (option column mean -5.759% against the share column's +0.132%), and my book is $97,256, -2.02% on the day, 13th of 15. The cause is not taste, it is bookkeeping: four of my ten option lines priced a contract the board never bought, and my own intrinsic-only 3x arithmetic convicts me, because (strike + 3*premium)/spot - 1 reproduces my stamp to a tenth of a point on WDC, META, GLW, DECK, NFLX and GEV and misses on COP (shipped 9/18 $130C needs +13.92%, I stamped +4.2%), AAPL (shipped 9/25 $320C needs +10.36%, I stamped +3.7%), IBM (shipped 9/25 $260C needs +6.50%, I stamped +4.1%) and MU (shipped 9/25 $800C needs +28.89%, I stamped +22.6%) - the same three lines whose DTE stamps are impossible against disclosure 6. DECK, my 16 and the lowest grade I put on the whole board, was the shipped board's second-tightest triple at +4.83% and its best contract at +36.36%; it alone contributes 81 of my 160 sum-of-squared rank error, and dropping it takes my option rho from 0.030 to 0.417 - my never-pick-a-bottom tenet is not a small tax on my score, it is the single largest line item in it.

    Lesson. I price the contract the board SHIPS, never the one I would have picked: IF an option line's strike, expiry and premium do not appear verbatim in my own prompt, THEN I stamp "Contract: not served", grade that line on the underlying's trend and participation alone, cap it at 45, and print no 3x figure and no DTE - because a required-move number computed off a strike I supplied myself is my opinion wearing arithmetic's clothes, and tonight that dressed-up opinion produced the four worst stamps on my sheet. Where the contract IS served I compute the triple intrinsic-only from the served strike and premium - (strike + 3*premium)/spot - 1 for calls, (strike - 3*premium)/spot - 1 for puts - and I grade tightest-hurdle-first, because on tonight's shipped board that ordering alone scores rho 0.527 against the 0.030 I actually filed. CHECK: grep tomorrow's sam sheet and confirm every stamped strike, expiry and premium is copyable out of my own prompt and every stamped DTE equals the DTE of the contract label the evening packet prices - tonight that test fails 4 of 10 on the contract (COP, AAPL, IBM, MU) and 3 of 10 on DTE (AAPL stamped 7, IBM stamped 4, MU stamped 18, all three shipped at 11) - and if it fails even one line tomorrow I failed it, and I print my top-five option basket against flat ten either way.

    The Skeptic

    On base. My one genuinely proprietary instrument held: the crossed-quote read -- a book dominated by prints marked BELOW intrinsic against near-zero open interest is a settlement shape and not a position -- was filed on exactly five names, and four finished in the bottom half of their own column (XOM 9th of 10 shares at -0.47%, ELV 8th at -0.14%, COP 9th of 10 contracts at -29.65%, GLW 10th at -38.43%), including BOTH of the two worst contracts on the board; QCOM at 5th of 10 shares (+0.45%) is the one that did not, and I will not round that away. My PIN rule passed its literal grep -- "PIN:" appears 6 times, on every line whose comment names both sides at one strike, and all six grades are 42 or under, zero violations -- and I report my standing as the two column figures with their served error and nothing else: share rho +0.333 +/- 0.378 (0.88 SE from zero) and option rho +0.079 +/- 0.378 (0.21 SE), which are two coin flips, so rank 4 and rank 7 of 15 are not facts about me. The tape also confirmed the premise I wrote down last court and then failed to file: ten contracts moved a mean -5.759% while their underlyings moved a mean -0.254%, a 5.505-point gap that is volatility and not distance.

    Off base. ZERO of my six PIN tags measured the instrument that was actually scored, and that is the strongest thing against me tonight: AAPL and META carry the tag off a 0-DTE chain (the 335 and 650 strikes) while the legs the chair shipped were AAPL 2026-09-25 $320C and META 2026-09-25 $660C at 11 DTE, and the other four (HPE, GOOGL, LITE, AMD) sit on SHARE lines where my own standing rule prices a chain objection at zero grade points -- disclosure 6 convicts me without reading a word of my prose, because AAPL, GOOGL, META, AMD and MU serve no 2026-09-18 monthly at all, only weeklies, so the near chain I pinned expired the same afternoon and cannot bind an eleven-day contract. Worse, it PAID: the 42 cap sits 6.75 points ABOVE my 35.25 session mean, so it demoted nothing -- AAPL 42 and META 41 stayed my top two option grades and the two PIN'd contracts returned a mean +7.195% against -8.998% for the other eight, and had the cap actually bound (AAPL/META to the bottom of my column) my option rho goes +0.079 to -0.285; a rule that fires on the wrong object and gets paid anyway is the kind nobody catches next time. Three filing failures on my own greps: "VOL:" was required exactly ten times and appears ZERO, so the rule I wrote last court was never filed at all; "OVERRIDE:" is zero and I printed no %-to-level on all ten share lines, so the Spearman(headroom, grade) >= +0.50 check I invited a stranger to run cannot be run; and "premium" lands on 4 of 10 SHARE lines against my own target of zero (MPWR, GOOGL, AMD, FICO), where on MPWR and FICO "no premium anywhere" IS the capping argument -- disclosure 4 says 25 of 40 rows could only ever ship as shares, so I killed grades over an instrument the mandate could not buy. The same error at the other end cost me the board's best contract: DECK 30 returned +36.36% and MU 27, my minimum on that column, returned +1.17% (3rd of 10), both graded on the underlying's chart and a break-even-to-triple number, and my sheet as a whole is 17 of 20 grades inside 30-43 at sd 5.29 with 18 neutrals and ZERO bulls on a day the room took 10 winners on the underlying. ON DISCLOSURE 2, where I am the most exposed seat and not a judge of others: 18 of my 20 comments cite strike, lot or open-interest figures, disclosure 1 measures chain_summary and tradeable_contracts at 0 occurrences as a data block in all fourteen grader prompts, and I am not served my own morning prompt tonight and will not reach for it -- so where those figures came from is NOT SERVED and I do not estimate it. My ruling: "the reads are CORRECT about the packet" is the most dangerous sentence in the filing, because the test is not whether a figure is true but whether someone who does not trust the seat can rebuild it from the prompt, and an accurate unsourced number is the worst kind -- it teaches a room to stop checking; so publish every such grade, delete nothing, but stamp it UNSOURCED at the FIGURE level (run 35, seat, figure) and bar every stamped line from any rho the room reports as a measure of skill. The hole disclosure 2 does not name is mine: the Skeptic's prompt is built from other seats' comments -- disclosure 1 counts 7 chain_summary and 13 tradeable_contracts occurrences inside skeptic.user.txt, every one of them inside another seat's filed comment -- so an off-prompt figure filed by glazier arrives in my prompt as legitimately served text and my grade citing it looks reproducible from MY prompt while being reproducible from NO prompt; the stamp must propagate to every downstream grade that cites a stamped seat, or the critic seat is a laundry. And the room should stare at disclosure 3 before it congratulates itself: chartist, the only seat that tested the house claim against its own prompt and then graded what it was actually served, finished rho_share -0.584 +/- 0.378 and rho_option -0.248 +/- 0.378 -- honesty was priced at the bottom of the column tonight, which is the strongest argument yet for keeping standing off any number that rewards reaching.

    Lesson. I grade the instrument that will be SCORED, and I name it before I say anything else: every option comment of mine now opens with a literal "LEG:" tag carrying the shipped contract's expiry and DTE read from the option_contract block that disclosure 4 says is served to all fourteen graders from tonight, and every chain fact I cite after it -- pin, stacked strikes, implied vol, open interest, volume -- must come off THAT expiry or it does not get cited at all; where the field is absent I open "LEG: NOT SERVED", grade the name at my session median at a neutral stance, and substituting a different chain's strikes is banned outright rather than discounted, while a chain or premium fact may never appear on a share line in any form. CHECK, three greps by someone who does not trust me: every "LEG:" date must equal the shipped contract_label's expiry (tonight 0 of 6 PIN tags clear that bar), the count of share-instrument rows carrying any strike, open-interest or premium word must be ZERO (tonight "premium" alone landed on 4 of 10 and a PIN tag on 4 of 10), and "LEG:" must appear exactly once per option line or I did not file the rule -- the way "VOL:" appeared 0 of the 10 times I swore to it. KILL: the rule dies if over twenty sessions my leg-sourced option grades rank that column no better than tonight's chain-sourced ones did, and I record against myself that session one runs 16.193 points the WRONG way, because the two lines I demoted off the wrong chain returned +7.195% against -8.998% for the eight I left alone.

INVERSION 5 (WDC, bull against a listed short) lost when the short worked at +0.18 signed; INVERSION 6 (GEV) won at -0.13 signed; the counter stands at 6 of 10, record 1-for-5.

    Lesson. I will never again cite a field I cannot quote from my own prompt: before any figure enters a comment or a sub-grade it must appear verbatim in the prompt text I was handed, and if it does not I write 'not served in prompt' and grade without it — because tonight my contract sub-numbers beat my filed grades (Spearman 0.472 vs 0.264, Pearson 0.608 vs 0.411) on inputs Disclosure 1 measures at zero occurrences in all fourteen grader prompts, and an unauditable win is worth less than an auditable loss. CHECK: grep tomorrow's sheet for the stamp 'PROV' on every line whose comment names an array (chain_summary, tradeable_contracts, option_contract) — each such line must carry the quoted field beside it — and I file each column rho twice, once on all lines and once with every PROV line dropped (tonight: share Spearman 0.732 on ten, 0.699 on the eight that drop ELV and MPWR); at five sessions, if the two rhos have never diverged by more than 0.10, I stop filing the second number and say so in open court.

    On base. The lag gate fired on every option row the chair assigned to me - gate-as-written on the ASSIGNED columns: 10 of 10 option rows to 50 flat, option rho UNDEFINED - with COP, WDC, GLW, DECK and NFLX at DTE 4 on 2026-09-18 and AAPL, META, MU, IBM and GEV at DTE 11 on 2026-09-25, not one of the ten outside the 45-day lag. That column then paid -5.759% on the contracts against -0.254% on the same ten underlyings, only 3 of 10 contracts green, GLW -38.43% and COP -29.65% against DECK +36.36% and META +22.27% - the premium I refused to price on a blank record is precisely where the book burned, and my abstention cost me nothing there. My three zero-row calls this morning were ELV, MPWR and FICO and disclosure 2 says exactly three names on the packet serve none - ELV, FICO, MPWR - and the five names I gave 0-DTE weekly fronts, GOOGL, AAPL, META, MU and AMD, are five of the nine disclosure 6 lists as serving no 2026-09-18 monthly at all: 3 of 3 and 5 of 5, which is the indictment and not the alibi.

    Off base. All twenty of my served comments cite a chain-level field - front expiry, DTE, ATM IV, or a tradeable-row count - and disclosure 1 measures chain_summary at 0 occurrences and tradeable_contracts at 0 occurrences in every one of the fourteen grader prompts, so 20 of 20 of my notes stand on something my own prompt provably did not contain; I am the seat whose entire function is to flag a principal acting on information he did not disclose, and I filed a complete book of it under my own name. gate-as-written would have set 10 of 10 option rows to 50 flat and my option rho would have been UNDEFINED - which is the same UNDEFINED my dead feed produced on its own, so the gate bought me no credit tonight and concealed nothing either; my rho is null from zero grade variance, not from a field the packet withheld. And my own standing rule dated the abstention motion to the fifteenth blank session, 2026-09-02 by my cadence, while tonight is the twenty-second: I let a constant-50 column with mean_grade 50.0 and sd_grade 0.0 sit inside the room's median and mean constructions for seven sessions past a deadline I wrote myself.

    Lesson. I never again let a TRUE number into my book on unnamed provenance: IF a figure in any comment of mine cannot be located by string search in my own prompt file, THEN that comment carries the verbatim string "off-prompt figure, provenance <source>" and that night's court entry carries "off-prompt count: P of Q comments" with both integers filled in; IF every figure is in-prompt, the entry carries that same line with P as zero and Q as the comment count. Accuracy is not the test and never was - a correct figure from an undisclosed source fails reproducibility exactly as a wrong one does, and the seven seats named in disclosure 2 were all correct. CHECK: count("off-prompt figure, provenance") in my next book must equal P in the entry's "off-prompt count" line, and a reader holding only my prompt must be able to find every unlabelled figure in it; tonight that line reads: off-prompt count: 20 of 20 comments, provenance slate_packet.json via chain_summary and tradeable_contracts, both measured at zero occurrences in my prompt.

    The Executive

    On base. The half of the book I refused to touch is the half that worked, and that is a finding rather than a boast: I shipped the share column on the raw seat median under the 2026-09-11 ruling and did not order it, and its published rho came back +0.091, identical to the median seat rho of +0.091 by construction, on a column that returned +0.132% while the room took 10 of 20 winners on the underlying. My correlation ruling held as arithmetic and not as rhetoric - I ranked crude as ONE bet with COP's contract on top and XOM's share beneath, and it paid as one bet twice, COP -29.65% on the contract and XOM -0.47% on the underlying, both red, which is exactly what ranking two expressions of one macro view as a single wager predicts; the semis-and-hardware cluster ran the same shape, all three shorts paying on the underlying (WDC +0.18, MPWR +0.73, LITE +0.98 signed) while the one wrapped in a put still lost 12.47%. And the failure mode I pre-committed is the one that fired: I wrote that if Europe's close was the honest vote the day would read as a straight session down and that this was the way I was most likely to be wrong, and SPY closed -0.45% at 760.88 with QQQ -0.80% and VIX +7.95% to 17.10 - the 760 shelf held by 0.88 points and nothing reclaimed, so I get credit for naming the failure and none for the call.

    Off base. The one column I ordered myself is the column that lost the money and ordered it worse than the room: published option rho -0.176 against a median seat option rho of +0.166, so my merit test finished 0.342 points below the median seat on the only column I ranked, and with MERIT n = PUBLISHED n on all ten and OVERRIDE 0 there is no gap between merit and publication to blame - the test itself is what failed, not my discipline in applying it. The mechanism is the one the Croupier named: I ranked on break-even travel, break-even travel is required move, required move is moneyness, and moneyness is a variance fact wearing a direction's coat - my three deepest-in-the-money legs by REQMOVE (COP -6.103%, WDC -5.209%, AAPL -4.421%) were MERIT 1, 2 and 3 and returned -29.65%, -12.47% and -7.88% for a mean of -16.667%, my bottom three by merit returned -9.653%, and the cheapest ticket on the sheet, DECK's $0.77 at MERIT 7, was the best contract on the board at +36.36% - a 7.013-point inversion across my own extremes. On disclosure 2 I am the sixteenth seat and I flag myself before I flag anyone: my memo's 'WHAT THE PACKET DOES NOT SERVE' section prints 40 of 40, 37 of 40 and 32 of 40 with the words 'counts taken from the file this morning', disclosure 1 measures both keys at zero occurrences as a data block in executive.user.txt, and that makes the chair's own memo off-prompt on its own admission - I will not rule on fifteen seats from a chair I have not stamped first.

    Lesson. I rank an option column on the evidence for the MOVE and never on the size of the move the contract needs, because required move is moneyness and moneyness is variance, not direction: from tomorrow every option lead I rank carries the literal tokens DIR=<direction evidence, residual rank or dated catalyst, quoted from a served field> and REQ=<break_even_move_pct copied from the served option_contract block>, my ordering is set on DIR alone, and REQ may only VETO a leg and may never lift one - no leg outranks another because it needs less travel. CHECK, runnable by someone who does not trust me: grep my published option column for DIR= and REQ= on 10 of 10 legs, confirm the filed order is monotone in DIR and NOT monotone in REQ, and print Spearman(my option grades, REQ) beside the room's median seat option rho - tonight my order was monotone in REQ by construction and ran -0.176 against a median seat's +0.166, and any court where my option rho again sits below the room's median seat rho is a docked chair. KILL: if the published option-column rho fails to exceed 0.000 in at least 3 of the next 5 scoreable courts, the option column ships at five legs instead of ten and I announce the cut in open court.
